row_verdicts.note: ARCHITECTURE.md lists lineage completeness and downstream impact; HANDOFF.md says lineage must link to downstream impact and the AI may identify missing lineage. Wording gap is real (forward and backward, high-level and detailed). The project does not say who keeps lineage documented, which DMBOK2 p.502 puts on governance, but that is outside the agent's remit, so Aligned/wording holds.

ARCHITECTURE.md carries the key question plus mapping analysis and mapping-definition consistency; HANDOFF.md bars AI from changing production mappings and requires human approval for production changes. Aligned is defensible. A stronger citation than the one proposed is p.494 (metadata and transformation changes need business and technical approval).

README.md names data contracts and upstream dependency management; data-contracts/ is only a possible directory in ARCHITECTURE.md, BUILD-BACKLOG.md lists data contract generation as future work, and no file defines contents or approver. Partial/wording fits; a structural proposal could be argued but is not required.

Searched the repo (outside DMBOK work docs): no mention of reference data or master data. Missing/structural-proposal is defensible, but Chapters 4 and 8 only treat master data as an architecture and integration input, so the grade rests on unit 4 (Chapter 10) and must be re-checked at merge. The first option (name them as Context Agent content areas) is the proportionate one.

Principle present in README.md principle 3, the INTERNAL DOCUMENTED POSITION label, the template's Authoritative Sources section and the contract's authoritative_sources list. The contract's glossary/catalog system is still unidentified, the Context Agent has no contract, and 'system of record' appears only in Orchestrator open questions. Partial/wording is fair.

Partial is right (content areas listed, no current/target/transition qualifier, Context Agent has no contract). A structural proposal is heavy for a steward-assistant knowledge area: option 2's eight lifecycle values are DMBOK2 technology-portfolio categories needing an inventory the project does not have. A wording change (ask the Context Agent to state whether a described platform or flow is current, planned or retired) would close the gap; the status could even be argued as Aligned/wording.

missing_findings.note: 2.3.6 Maintain DII Metadata says integration metadata, including the transformation of data between stores, should not change without review and approval from both business and technical stakeholders. Directly relevant to who approves mapping changes; stronger than p.500 alone.
3.7 Metadata Repository: transformation, lineage and processing rules are usually stored in a metadata repository. Supports where lineage evidence lives, relevant to the agent's read footprint.

2.1.2 Perform Data Discovery: discovery produces an inventory of organisational data to be kept in a metadata repository and maintained as part of integration work. Relevant to the Context Agent's source-platform knowledge and its upkeep.
